question: The birdie (shuttlecock) of badminton is made up of 16 feathers, it is between 62-70 mm long and weighs between _____.
solution:
The correct answer is __**4.74 and 5.5 g**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **birdie (shuttlecock)** used in badminton is a high-quality projectile made with **16 feathers**, typically sourced from a goose or duck. 
 
• The shuttlecock has a standard length of **62-70 mm**, ensuring uniformity in play and compliance with international badminton regulations. 
 
• The official weight range of the shuttlecock is **4.74 to 5.5 grams**, as specified by the **Badminton World Federation (BWF)**. This weight ensures optimal flight stability and aerodynamics. 
 
• The feather structure of the shuttlecock provides precision in flight and is designed for high-speed gameplay. The unique design ensures it decelerates faster than most projectiles in sports. 
 
• The shuttlecock undergoes rigorous testing for weight and balance before being approved for professional matches, making the range of **4.74 to 5.5 grams** a critical specification.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Badminton Shuttlecock Design:**

 
 
• The shuttlecock consists of a **cork base**, typically covered with a thin layer of leather, which provides structural integrity and weight.
 
• The feathers are arranged in a circular pattern, glued to the cork base, and carefully trimmed to maintain balance and flight consistency.
 
• Most shuttlecocks used in professional tournaments are made of **goose feathers**, as they are more durable and provide better flight characteristics compared to synthetic ones.
 
• Modern shuttlecocks are tested for **speed, trajectory, and stability** under specific conditions to ensure compatibility with international standards.
 
 
 
• **Badminton World Federation (BWF) Regulations:**
 
 
• The **BWF** governs all aspects of badminton, including specifications for equipment such as shuttlecocks, rackets, and court dimensions.
 
• Shuttlecock weight and design are critical for maintaining fairness and uniform gameplay across tournaments worldwide.
 
• Shuttlecocks are categorized into different speeds (slow, medium, fast) to adapt to varying conditions like altitude and temperature during gameplay.
 
 
 
• **Feather Shuttlecock vs Synthetic Shuttlecock:**
 
 
• **Feather shuttlecocks** are preferred for professional play due to their precision and ability to decelerate quickly after being hit.
 
• **Synthetic shuttlecocks** are more durable and cost-effective but do not offer the same flight characteristics as feathered ones. They are commonly used in recreational play.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts about Badminton:**
 
 
• Badminton originated in **Pune, India**, during the British colonial era and was initially referred to as "Poona."
 
• The **first official badminton rules** were established in **1877** by the Bath Badminton Club in England.
 
• Badminton became an **Olympic sport** in **1992**, with events for singles, doubles, and mixed doubles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shuttlecock Testing:**

 
 
• Shuttlecock testing involves ensuring that it flies consistently through the air and lands within specific areas when hit with a standard force.
 
• The testing process includes verifying the weight, feather arrangement, and cork dimensions.
 
 
 
• **Professional Use:**
 
 
• Feathered shuttlecocks are exclusively used in **international tournaments** sanctioned by the BWF.
 
• Recreational players often use synthetic shuttlecocks to reduce costs and enhance durability.
